_comment: Measurements and estimates of the K-shaped economy published by others, for section 08 of the American Consumer page. Curated in a session; every figure was read in the document its `url` opens (or, when `via` names an intermediary, in that intermediary's text) and carries its period and publication date. `kind`: private = a third-party estimate (badged as such, never mixed into an official series); fed = research by the Federal Reserve Board or a Reserve Bank; official = a statistic or prototype of a federal statistical agency. `measure: spendTop10` puts the figure in the chart that compares the top 10%'s share of spending across measurements (`measureLabel` is its bar label, `rank` says how households are ranked); `superseded: true` marks a figure its publisher later revised. `headline: true` marks the one estimate quoted in the section's stat row and summary. Quotes are short and shown in their original language. `reviewed` is the date of the last pass.

via.en: as reported by Bloomberg Opinion (Justin Fox)

note.en: Not a count of purchases: Moody's estimates each income group's saving from the Federal Reserve's financial accounts and its survey of family finances, and treats the disposable income left over (personal outlays) as spending. Four-quarter moving average; figure after a change of method to reflect taxes.
note.es: No es un conteo de compras: Moody's estima el ahorro de cada grupo de ingreso con las cuentas financieras de la Reserva Federal y su encuesta de finanzas familiares, y trata como gasto el ingreso disponible restante (desembolsos personales). Promedio móvil de cuatro trimestres; cifra posterior a un cambio de método para reflejar los impuestos.

estimates.publisher: Federal Reserve Board, FEDS Notes (Aladangady, Bricker, Chang, Goodman and Li)

note.en: From the 2025 survey's measure of family spending (the note's chart measures spending other than housing). The survey oversamples wealthy families, whom household spending surveys cover poorly; the same share holds ranking families by wealth. The top 1% of spenders do 9% of spending, against 19% of income and 32% of wealth for the top 1% of each.
note.es: Con la medición del gasto familiar de la encuesta de 2025 (la gráfica de la nota mide el gasto distinto de vivienda). La encuesta sobremuestrea a las familias ricas, que las encuestas de gasto cubren mal; la participación es la misma al ordenar a las familias por riqueza. El 1% que más gasta hace el 9% del gasto, frente a 19% del ingreso y 32% de la riqueza del 1% superior de cada uno.

label.en: Share of consumption of the top 20% of earners, a variant of the Moody's method that deducts taxes
label.es: Parte del consumo del 20% de mayor ingreso, con una variante del método de Moody's que descuenta impuestos

estimates.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas (Benjamin Hoham and Fang Yang)

note.en: 53% on average in 1990–99: by this measure concentration is high but rose 4 points in three decades. The authors note that in the BEA and BLS joint distribution of income and consumption the top 10% of earners do roughly 20% of consumption and the top 20% about 35%, stable since 2004.
note.es: 53% en promedio en 1990–99: con esta medida la concentración es alta pero subió 4 puntos en tres décadas. Los autores señalan que en la distribución conjunta de ingreso y consumo de la BEA y la BLS el 10% de mayor ingreso hace cerca de 20% del consumo y el 20% superior cerca de 35%, estable desde 2004.
